readme:
# GitHub Repository Search Scraper

Search public GitHub repositories and export one row per repository: name, owner, description, stars, forks, watchers, open issues, language, topics, license, dates, flags and more. You pay per repository delivered.

The data comes from the documented public [GitHub](https://github.com/) search interface (`api.github.com/search/repositories`). No GitHub account and no access token are needed. The actor does not ask for a token and never sends one.

## What you get

For each repository the actor returns one row with:

- `id`, `nodeId`, `name`, `fullName`, `url`, `apiUrl`, `description`
- `ownerLogin`, `ownerId`, `ownerType` (User or Organization), `ownerUrl`, `ownerAvatarUrl`: public owner details only
- `stars`, `forks`, `watchers`, `openIssues` (open issues and pull requests, as GitHub counts them)
- `language`, `topics`
- `licenseSpdx`, `licenseName`, `licenseKey`
- `defaultBranch`, `sizeKb`
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `pushedAt`: times in UTC
- `homepage`
- `archived`, `disabled`, `isFork`, `isTemplate`, `isPrivate`, `isMirror`, `mirrorUrl`, `allowForking`, `webCommitSignoffRequired`
- `hasIssues`, `hasProjects`, `hasDownloads`, `hasWiki`, `hasPages`, `hasDiscussions`
- `visibility`, `score` (GitHub's relevance score for the search)
- `cloneUrl`, `sshUrl`, `gitUrl`
- `rank` (position in the results of the search), `query` (the search text used), `sourceUrl`, `scrapedAt`

A value the source does not show is null. Topics is an empty list when a repository has none.

## Typical uses

- Find the most starred projects on a topic, in a language, or in a time window
- Track new and recently updated projects in a field
- Build lists of open source tools with their licenses and activity
- Find sponsors, partners or hiring targets through the organizations behind popular projects
- Feed a dashboard, a spreadsheet or a research dataset

## Pricing

You pay per repository delivered, plus a small fee for each run.

| Event | Name | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Run start (charged once, together with the first delivered row) | `actor-start` | $0.001 per run |
| One repository row | `repository-result` | $0.001 per repository ($1.00 per 1,000) |

A run that finds nothing is not charged. If you set a maximum cost for the run, the actor stops cleanly once the next row would go over it.

**New to Apify?** Every account gets a $5 free monthly platform credit, enough for a first test run before you pay anything.

## Limits you should know

- GitHub allows 10 searches per minute without a sign-in. Each page of up to 100 repositories is one search. The actor reads the limit that GitHub reports and, when no search is left, waits for the reset (up to 65 seconds) and continues.
- GitHub returns at most 1,000 results for any search (10 pages of 100). When a search reaches that limit, the run status says so. To get more, split the work into several searches with narrower filters, for example `stars:100..500` and `stars:501..2000`, or one search per language.
- How long a run takes: up to 10 pages arrive without a long pause, so 1,000 repositories take about one to two minutes. Each further group of 10 pages adds about one minute of waiting. For example 5 searches of 1,000 repositories each take roughly 5 to 6 minutes. The actor reads one page every 3 seconds.
- GitHub sometimes marks an answer as incomplete when its own search timed out. The run status says so when this happens.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `queries` | list | `topic:web-scraping` | One GitHub search text per line. Raw GitHub search syntax works, for example `topic:web-scraping stars:>100`, `language:go pushed:>2026-01-01` or `web crawler in:name,description` |
| `language` | text | empty | Adds `language:<name>` to every search |
| `minStars` | number | 0 | Adds `stars:>=N` to every search |
| `topic` | list | empty | Adds `topic:<name>` to every search. A repository must carry all listed topics |
| `sort` | choice | `stars` | `stars`, `updated`, `forks` or `best` (best match) |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | number | 100 | Repositories per search text, up to 1,000 |

How it works:

- Every search text is read in turn, page by page, in the order GitHub gives (the `sort` you chose).
- Filters are added to every search text. A filter the text already holds is not added twice.
- With no search text, the filters make one search. With no input at all, the actor searches the topic `web-scraping`.
- A repository that matches two searches is delivered once, with the first search that found it.
- Number fields also accept numbers written as text, for example `"150"`.
- A search text that GitHub rejects as invalid is skipped and named in the status. The other searches continue.

### Example: popular web scraping projects

```json
{
  "queries": ["topic:web-scraping"],
  "sort": "stars",
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 150
}
```

### Example: Go projects with filters, two searches

```json
{
  "queries": ["web crawler", "headless browser automation"],
  "language": "Go",
  "minStars": 100,
  "sort": "updated",
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 200
}
```

## Limitations

- The actor reads repository search only. It does not read file contents, issues, commits, releases or user profiles.
- Owner details are the public login, id, type, page and avatar address. No names, emails or other profile data.
- `stars` and the other counts change often. A row shows the values at `scrapedAt`.
- The order of results can shift while repositories change, so a few repositories can be missed or repeated between two pages. Repeats are removed.
- `sizeKb` is the size GitHub reports, in kilobytes.
- If GitHub keeps answering with errors or keeps its request limit, the run stops with a status that says so, and only delivered rows are charged.

## FAQ

**Do I need a GitHub account or token?**
No. The actor uses GitHub's public search without a sign-in, which is why the limit is 10 searches per minute.

**Why are there at most 1,000 repositories per search?**
GitHub returns only the first 1,000 results of any search. Split the work into narrower searches, for example by star ranges, language or creation date.

**How do I write a search?**
Use GitHub's repository search syntax, for example `topic:web-scraping stars:>100`, `language:python created:>2026-01-01`, `user:apify` or `org:microsoft`. The `queries` field takes the same text you would type on github.com.

**Why did I get fewer rows than `maxResultsPerQuery`?**
The search matched fewer repositories, or the maximum cost you set for the run was reached. The run status message says which.

**What happens with a search that finds nothing?**
The run ends with no rows, nothing is charged, and the status says so.

**Can a run be restarted safely?**
Yes. Progress is saved after every page. A restarted run continues where it stopped and does not deliver or charge the same rows twice.

**Is this affiliated with GitHub?**
No. This is an independent tool that reads GitHub's public search. Please keep your use modest and in line with GitHub's terms.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex.

**MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=nanodata/github-repository-search-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**
